## The Art (and Science) of Plotting

### Plot Types

ggplot2 allows the creation of various plot types for data visualization, each serving a different analytical purpose.

Bar plots, dot plots, and line plots are commonly used to visualize frequencies, counts, and proportions.
![Bar-Plot](/Users/patrickblumrich/Bildschirmfotos/Bar_Plot.png)
![Dot-Plot](/Users/patrickblumrich/Bildschirmfotos/Dot_Plot.png)
![Line-Plot](/Users/patrickblumrich/Bildschirmfotos/Line_Plot.png)

Several visualization options are available for continuous data, depending on the type of information that should be emphasized.
Histograms and density plots are commonly used to visualize the distribution of continuous data.
![Histogram](/Users/patrickblumrich/Bildschirmfotos/Histogram.png)
![Density-Plot](/Users/patrickblumrich/Bildschirmfotos/Density_Plot.png)

Box plots and violin plots are commonly used to compare summary statistics across groups.
![Box-Plot](/Users/patrickblumrich/Bildschirmfotos/Box_Plot.png)
![Violin-Plot](/Users/patrickblumrich/Bildschirmfotos/Violin_Plot.png)

Scatter plots are commonly used to visualize relationships between two numeric variables.
![Scatter-Plot](/Users/patrickblumrich/Bildschirmfotos/Scatter_Plot.png)
